reason: The code itself checks out on the 65SC12. The new high-byte sequence gives (p_hi AND 3)<<4 | p_lo>>4, 24 cycles against 28. The EOR table equals (n EOR &1F) OR channel_bits for all 4 channels. The amplitude cache is safe: request hi bytes are &A5/&A6, sfx_silence and .ended leave sfx_n=0 until a request re-marks the cache, there is no data byte without a latch, and OSWORD 7 is only reached with irq_owned clear. The next write enable falls 39 cycles or more after WE high on every path, including sfx_silence's loop at about 45. Y now leaves sfx_write as 8 instead of 0 and Z=0, but no caller reads either. The size is what fails. In the region I recount 77 -> 90 bytes, +13, because old lines 186-195 (14 bytes) stay in place unreachable. That fits the shipping build: andy_load &AFF6 + &FF9 = &BFEF leaves 17 bytes, so 4 after the change. It does not fit the gameplay disc. build/strykers-gameplay.symbols.json (built 2026-10-23 01:23 from this branch, the same time as the shipping build) has andy_load &AFFC, so bank 5 ends at &BFF5 with 11 bytes free. +13 overruns by 2, the main.6502:187 ASSERT ('bank 5 overruns its 16K') fails, and the published gameplay build no longer assembles. The gate only builds the shipping flag set, so it would not catch this. Deleting the 14 dead bytes (lines 186-195; the .noise path does not use them) would make it -1 byte and save the candidate.
